messages:
Aisha (CEO): Leaving this thread for follow-ups from the all-hands about positioning and the GTM playbook. I'll answer short Qs here.
Mina (sales): Top ask: what's the simplest way to explain our mission to exec buyers in 20s?
Aisha (CEO): 20s pitch: 'Redwood makes advanced LLMs behave like a predictable product: consistent latency, transparent unit economics, and deployment choices that meet compliance and SLA needs.' Short, outcome-first.
Sergio (Head of GTM): For sales decks, should we lead with benchmarks or with deployment options? Which resonates more with enterprise buyers?
Tom (VP Product): Start with deployment and SLO story for enterprises (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Follow with a single benchmark slide that shows cost/latency improvement for a representative workload.
Mina (sales): Competitor framing: how do we differentiate from 'managed endpoints' from cloud providers without naming them?
Aisha (CEO): Focus on productized inference vs infrastructure: 'We deliver inference as a product with SLAs, rollout controls, quality monitoring, and cost levers. Cloud endpoints are raw infrastructure.' Keep it factual.
Arun (eng): Technical Q for messaging: can we claim 'lower cost by design' or is that risky?
Leah (legal): Claim must be verifiable. Use 'lower cost in many production workloads due to batching, caching, and quantization' and avoid absolute language. Provide links to internal benchmarks we can cite.
Sergio (Head of GTM): For buyer objections around vendor lock-in, quick line?
Aisha (CEO): 'We provide portable deployment options and model/version pinning so you retain control. Many customers start with hosted and migrate to Dedicated or Private when ready.'
Mina (sales): Any standard objection response for 'why not self-host open models'?
Aisha (CEO): 'Self-hosting is a multi-year engineering project. We deliver operational primitives (KV caching, optimized kernels, rollout tooling, and cost monitoring) that most teams don't want to build and maintain.'
Arun (eng): Roadmap ask: will we invest in cross-region routing vs single-region resilience first?
Tom (VP Product): Prioritize single-region resilience and predictable latency; cross-region routing follows once we have mature fallback and capacity policies.
Sergio (Head of GTM): Can we get a 1-page battlecard with approved lines and SLO templates?
Aisha (CEO): Yes 1. Battlecard with approved messaging, SLO templates, and a sanitized benchmark will be published to the sales drive before EOD.
slides-bot: Slides and recording uploaded: https://internal.redwood.example/all-hands/1777654322 :white_check_mark:
Mina (sales): Thanks! I'll review and give feedback.
Aisha (CEO): Great. If anyone wants to workshop objection handling or customer roleplay, DM me or Sergio. Closing thread. 44D
